title: Transversals & Parallel Lines
description: When a transversal crosses two parallel lines, the angles pair up. Name the pair (corresponding, alternate interior, alternate exterior, same-side interior, vertical, linear pair), set up equal or add-to-180, and solve for x. Follows the IXL skill D.5 "Transversals of parallel lines: solve for x". Figures are described in words: the parallel lines run left to right and each angle is named by its crossing point, above or below the line, and left or right of the transversal.

practice.prompt:
Horizontal lines MN and OP are parallel, with MN above OP. From left to right, the points on MN are M, Q, N, and the points on OP are O, R, P. Transversal KL slopes down to the right, with K, Q, R, L in that order.
At Q, the angle below line MN and to the right of the transversal (∠NQR) measures (2x + 41)°.
At R, the angle above line OP and to the left of the transversal (∠ORQ) measures 51°.
Solve for x.
hints: Both angles are between the two parallel lines, and they are on opposite sides of the transversal. What pair is that?
They are alternate interior angles, so they are equal: 2x + 41 = 51.
Subtract 41 from both sides, then divide by 2.
practice.solution:
Both angles are inside the parallel lines, on opposite sides of KL → alternate interior angles → equal.
2x + 41 = 51
2x = 10
x = 5

figure.alt: Parallel lines MN and OP cut by transversal KL at Q and R. At Q, angle NQR (below MN, right of KL) is labeled 2x + 41 degrees. At R, angle ORQ (above OP, left of KL) is labeled 51 degrees.

practice.prompt: Horizontal lines m and n are parallel, with m above n. Transversal t crosses m at point P and n at point R. At P, the angle above m and to the right of t measures (3x + 15)°. At R, the angle above n and to the right of t measures 75°. Solve for x.
hints: Both angles are in the same spot at their crossing (above the line, right of t). What pair is that?
Corresponding angles are equal: 3x + 15 = 75.
practice.solution:
Same position at each crossing → corresponding angles → equal.
3x + 15 = 75
3x = 60
x = 20

figure.alt: Parallel lines m and n cut by transversal t at P and R. At P, the angle above the line, right of the transversal is labeled (3x + 15) degrees. At R, the angle above the line, right of the transversal is labeled 75 degrees.

practice.prompt: Horizontal lines m and n are parallel, with m above n. Transversal t crosses m at point P and n at point R. At P, the angle above m and to the left of t measures (4x − 8)°. At R, the angle below n and to the right of t measures 112°. Solve for x.
hints: Both angles are outside the parallel lines, on opposite sides of t. What pair is that?
Alternate exterior angles are equal: 4x − 8 = 112.
practice.solution:
Outside the lines, opposite sides of t → alternate exterior angles → equal.
4x − 8 = 112
4x = 120
x = 30

figure.alt: Parallel lines m and n cut by transversal t at P and R. At P, the angle above the line, left of the transversal is labeled (4x − 8) degrees. At R, the angle below the line, right of the transversal is labeled 112 degrees.

practice.prompt: Horizontal lines m and n are parallel, with m above n. Transversal t crosses m at point P and n at point R. At P, the angle below m and to the right of t measures (5x + 10)°. At R, the angle above n and to the right of t measures 95°. Solve for x.
hints: Both angles are between the parallel lines, on the same side of t. What pair is that?
Same-side (consecutive) interior angles are supplementary: (5x + 10) + 95 = 180.
practice.solution:
Between the lines, same side of t → same-side interior angles → add to 180°.
5x + 10 + 95 = 180
5x + 105 = 180
5x = 75
x = 15

figure.alt: Parallel lines m and n cut by transversal t at P and R. At P, the angle below the line, right of the transversal is labeled (5x + 10) degrees. At R, the angle above the line, right of the transversal is labeled 95 degrees.

practice.prompt: Horizontal lines m and n are parallel, with m above n. Transversal t crosses m at point P and n at point R. At P, the angle above m and to the left of t measures (x + 48)°, and the angle below m and to the right of t measures (3x − 12)°. Solve for x.
hints: Both angles are at the same point P and point in opposite directions. What pair is that?
Vertical angles are equal: x + 48 = 3x − 12.
Get the x's on one side: subtract x from both sides, then add 12.
practice.solution:
Opposite angles at the same crossing → vertical angles → equal.
x + 48 = 3x − 12
60 = 2x
x = 30

figure.alt: Parallel lines m and n cut by transversal t at P and R. At P, the angle above the line, left of the transversal is labeled (x + 48) degrees. At P, the angle below the line, right of the transversal is labeled (3x − 12) degrees.

practice.prompt: Horizontal lines m and n are parallel, with m above n. Transversal t crosses m at point P and n at point R. At P, the angle above m and to the left of t measures (2x + 30)°, and the angle above m and to the right of t measures 4x°. Solve for x.
hints: The two angles sit side by side on line m and share a side. What pair is that?
A linear pair adds to 180°: (2x + 30) + 4x = 180.
practice.solution:
Side by side on a straight line → linear pair → add to 180°.
2x + 30 + 4x = 180
6x + 30 = 180
6x = 150
x = 25

figure.alt: Parallel lines m and n cut by transversal t at P and R. At P, the angle above the line, left of the transversal is labeled (2x + 30) degrees. At P, the angle above the line, right of the transversal is labeled 4x degrees.

practice.prompt: Horizontal lines m and n are parallel, with m above n. Transversal t crosses m at point P and n at point R. At P, the angle below m and to the left of t measures (3x − 10)°. At R, the angle below n and to the left of t measures (x + 40)°. Solve for x.
hints: Same position at each crossing (below the line, left of t). What pair is that?
Corresponding angles are equal: 3x − 10 = x + 40.
Subtract x from both sides, then add 10 to both sides.
practice.solution:
Corresponding angles → equal.
3x − 10 = x + 40
2x − 10 = 40
2x = 50
x = 25 (each angle is 65°)

figure.alt: Parallel lines m and n cut by transversal t at P and R. At P, the angle below the line, left of the transversal is labeled (3x − 10) degrees. At R, the angle below the line, left of the transversal is labeled (x + 40) degrees.

practice.prompt: Horizontal lines m and n are parallel, with m above n. Transversal t crosses m at point P and n at point R. At P, the angle below m and to the left of t measures (5x − 22)°. At R, the angle above n and to the right of t measures (2x + 35)°. Solve for x.
hints: Both angles are between the lines, on opposite sides of t. What pair is that?
Alternate interior angles are equal: 5x − 22 = 2x + 35.
Subtract 2x from both sides, then add 22.
practice.solution:
Alternate interior angles → equal.
5x − 22 = 2x + 35
3x = 57
x = 19 (each angle is 73°)

figure.alt: Parallel lines m and n cut by transversal t at P and R. At P, the angle below the line, left of the transversal is labeled (5x − 22) degrees. At R, the angle above the line, right of the transversal is labeled (2x + 35) degrees.

practice.prompt: Horizontal lines m and n are parallel, with m above n. Transversal t crosses m at point P and n at point R. At P, the angle below m and to the left of t measures (4x + 12)°. At R, the angle above n and to the left of t measures (2x + 6)°. Find x. What is the measure of the (4x + 12)° angle, in degrees?
hints: Both angles are between the lines, on the same side of t. What pair is that?
Same-side interior angles add to 180°: (4x + 12) + (2x + 6) = 180.
After you find x, plug it into 4x + 12.
practice.solution:
Same-side interior → supplementary.
4x + 12 + 2x + 6 = 180
6x + 18 = 180
x = 27
4(27) + 12 = 120° (check: the other angle is 60°, and 120 + 60 = 180)

figure.alt: Parallel lines m and n cut by transversal t at P and R. At P, the angle below the line, left of the transversal is labeled (4x + 12) degrees. At R, the angle above the line, left of the transversal is labeled (2x + 6) degrees.

practice.prompt: Horizontal lines m and n are parallel, with m above n. Transversal t crosses m at point P and n at point R. At P, the angle above m and to the right of t measures (7x − 9)°. At R, the angle below n and to the left of t measures (4x + 27)°. Find x. What is the common measure of the two angles, in degrees?
hints: Both angles are outside the lines, on opposite sides of t. What pair is that?
Alternate exterior angles are equal: 7x − 9 = 4x + 27.
After you find x, plug it into either expression. Both should give the same number.

figure.alt: Parallel lines m and n cut by transversal t at P and R. At P, the angle above the line, right of the transversal is labeled (7x − 9) degrees. At R, the angle below the line, left of the transversal is labeled (4x + 27) degrees.

practice.prompt: Horizontal lines m and n are parallel, with m above n. Transversal t crosses m at point P and n at point R. At P, the angle above m and to the left of t measures (2x + 14)°. At R, the angle above n and to the right of t measures (x + 43)°. Solve for x.
hints: These two are not one of the named pairs directly. Use a middle angle: the angle at P above m and right of t.
That middle angle is corresponding to the (x + 43)° angle, so it equals x + 43. It also forms a linear pair with the (2x + 14)° angle.
practice.solution:
The angle at P above m, right of t, corresponds to the angle at R above n, right of t, so it is (x + 43)°.
It forms a linear pair with the (2x + 14)° angle:
2x + 14 + x + 43 = 180
3x + 57 = 180
3x = 123
x = 41 (the angles are 96° and 84°)

figure.alt: Parallel lines m and n cut by transversal t at P and R. At P, the angle above the line, left of the transversal is labeled (2x + 14) degrees. At R, the angle above the line, right of the transversal is labeled (x + 43) degrees.

practice.prompt: Horizontal lines m and n are parallel, with m above n. Transversal t crosses m at point P and n at point R. One angle is at P, below m and right of t. The other is at R, above n and left of t. What kind of angle pair is this?
hints: Are both angles between the parallel lines (interior) or outside them (exterior)?
Both are interior. Now: same side of t, or opposite sides?
practice.solution: Both are between m and n (interior), on opposite sides of t → Alternate interior angles.

figure.alt: Parallel lines m and n cut by transversal t at P and R. At P, the angle below the line, right of the transversal is labeled 1. At R, the angle above the line, left of the transversal is labeled 2.

practice.prompt: Horizontal lines m and n are parallel, with m above n. Transversal t crosses m at point P and n at point R. One angle is at P, above m and left of t. The other is at R, above n and left of t. What kind of angle pair is this?
hints: Compare the position of each angle at its own crossing.
Both are above their line and left of t: the same spot at each crossing.
practice.solution: Same spot at each crossing → Corresponding angles.

figure.alt: Parallel lines m and n cut by transversal t at P and R. At P, the angle above the line, left of the transversal is labeled 1. At R, the angle above the line, left of the transversal is labeled 2.

practice.prompt: Horizontal lines m and n are parallel, with m above n. Transversal t crosses m at point P and n at point R. Transversal t is not perpendicular to m or n. One angle is at P, below m and right of t. The other is at R, above n and right of t. How are their measures related?
hints: First name the pair: both are between the lines, on the same side of t.
Same-side interior angles are supplementary. Their measures add to 180°.
practice.solution: Between the lines, same side of t → same-side interior angles → They add to 180°.

figure.alt: Parallel lines m and n cut by transversal t at P and R. At P, the angle below the line, right of the transversal is labeled 1. At R, the angle above the line, right of the transversal is labeled 2.

practice.prompt: Horizontal lines m and n are parallel, with m above n. Transversal t crosses m at point P and n at point R. At P, the angle above m and to the right of t measures (9x − 20)°. At R, the angle above n and to the right of t measures (6x + 16)°. Find x. What is the common measure of the two angles, in degrees?
hints: Same position at each crossing. What pair is that?
Corresponding angles are equal: 9x − 20 = 6x + 16.
After you find x, plug it into either expression.

figure.alt: Parallel lines m and n cut by transversal t at P and R. At P, the angle above the line, right of the transversal is labeled (9x − 20) degrees. At R, the angle above the line, right of the transversal is labeled (6x + 16) degrees.

flashcards.back: A line that crosses two or more lines at different points. When it crosses two parallel lines, it makes 8 angles, 4 at each crossing.
Interior angles are between the two parallel lines. Exterior angles are outside them (above the top line or below the bottom line).
Same spot at each crossing (for example, above the line and right of the transversal at both). With parallel lines they are equal.
Between the parallel lines, on opposite sides of the transversal. With parallel lines they are equal. (They make a Z shape.)
Outside the parallel lines, on opposite sides of the transversal. With parallel lines they are equal.
Between the parallel lines, on the same side of the transversal. With parallel lines they are supplementary: they add to 180°. (They make a C or U shape.)
Opposite angles at the same crossing point. They are always equal, even without parallel lines.
Two angles side by side on a straight line, sharing a side. They always add to 180°.

1) Name the angle pair. 2) Equal pair → set the expressions equal. Supplementary pair → add them and set the sum to 180. 3) Solve. 4) Substitute x into the angle expressions. Check that each measure is greater than 0° and less than 180°, and that the measures are equal or add to 180°, as required.
If the transversal is not perpendicular, every acute angle in the figure is equal to every other acute angle, and every obtuse angle equals every other obtuse angle. Any acute + any obtuse = 180°.

quiz.prompt: Horizontal lines m and n are parallel, with m above n. Transversal t crosses m at point P and n at point R. At P, the angle below m and to the left of t measures (4x + 6)°. At R, the angle below n and to the left of t measures 70°. Solve for x.
hints: Same spot at each crossing. What pair is that?
Corresponding angles are equal: 4x + 6 = 70.

figure.alt: Parallel lines m and n cut by transversal t at P and R. At P, the angle below the line, left of the transversal is labeled (4x + 6) degrees. At R, the angle below the line, left of the transversal is labeled 70 degrees.

quiz.prompt: Horizontal lines m and n are parallel, with m above n. Transversal t crosses m at point P and n at point R. At P, the angle below m and to the left of t measures (6x − 15)°. At R, the angle above n and to the right of t measures (3x + 30)°. Solve for x.
hints: Between the lines, opposite sides of t. What pair is that?
Alternate interior angles are equal: 6x − 15 = 3x + 30.

figure.alt: Parallel lines m and n cut by transversal t at P and R. At P, the angle below the line, left of the transversal is labeled (6x − 15) degrees. At R, the angle above the line, right of the transversal is labeled (3x + 30) degrees.

quiz.prompt: Horizontal lines m and n are parallel, with m above n. Transversal t crosses m at point P and n at point R. At P, the angle below m and to the left of t measures (3x + 5)°. At R, the angle above n and to the left of t measures (2x + 25)°. Solve for x.
hints: Between the lines, same side of t. What pair is that?
Same-side interior angles add to 180°: (3x + 5) + (2x + 25) = 180.
quiz.solution:
Same-side interior → supplementary.
3x + 5 + 2x + 25 = 180
5x + 30 = 180
5x = 150
x = 30 (the angles are 95° and 85°)

figure.alt: Parallel lines m and n cut by transversal t at P and R. At P, the angle below the line, left of the transversal is labeled (3x + 5) degrees. At R, the angle above the line, left of the transversal is labeled (2x + 25) degrees.

quiz.prompt: Horizontal lines m and n are parallel, with m above n. Transversal t crosses m at point P and n at point R. At R, the angle above n and to the right of t measures (5x − 20)°, and the angle below n and to the left of t measures (2x + 46)°. Solve for x.
hints: Same point, opposite directions. What pair is that?
Vertical angles are equal: 5x − 20 = 2x + 46.

figure.alt: Parallel lines m and n cut by transversal t at P and R. At R, the angle above the line, right of the transversal is labeled (5x − 20) degrees. At R, the angle below the line, left of the transversal is labeled (2x + 46) degrees.

quiz.prompt: Horizontal lines m and n are parallel, with m above n. Transversal t crosses m at point P and n at point R. At R, the angle below n and to the left of t measures (7x + 12)°, and the angle below n and to the right of t measures (3x + 8)°. Solve for x.
hints: The angles sit side by side on line n and share a side. What pair is that?
A linear pair adds to 180°: (7x + 12) + (3x + 8) = 180.
quiz.solution:
Linear pair → supplementary.
7x + 12 + 3x + 8 = 180
10x + 20 = 180
x = 16 (the angles are 124° and 56°)

figure.alt: Parallel lines m and n cut by transversal t at P and R. At R, the angle below the line, left of the transversal is labeled (7x + 12) degrees. At R, the angle below the line, right of the transversal is labeled (3x + 8) degrees.

quiz.prompt: Horizontal lines m and n are parallel, with m above n. Transversal t crosses m at point P and n at point R. At P, the angle above m and to the left of t measures (8x − 5)°. At R, the angle below n and to the right of t measures (5x + 31)°. Find x. What is the common measure of the two angles, in degrees?
hints: Outside the lines, opposite sides of t. What pair is that?
Alternate exterior angles are equal: 8x − 5 = 5x + 31.
After you find x, plug it into either expression.

figure.alt: Parallel lines m and n cut by transversal t at P and R. At P, the angle above the line, left of the transversal is labeled (8x − 5) degrees. At R, the angle below the line, right of the transversal is labeled (5x + 31) degrees.

quiz.prompt: Horizontal lines m and n are parallel, with m above n. Transversal t crosses m at point P and n at point R. One angle is at P, above m and right of t. The other is at R, below n and left of t. What kind of angle pair is this?
hints: Are the angles between the lines or outside them?
Both are outside, on opposite sides of t.
quiz.solution: Outside m and n (exterior), opposite sides of t → Alternate exterior angles.

figure.alt: Parallel lines m and n cut by transversal t at P and R. At P, the angle above the line, right of the transversal is labeled 1. At R, the angle below the line, left of the transversal is labeled 2.

quiz.prompt: Horizontal lines m and n are parallel, with m above n. Transversal t crosses m at point P and n at point R. At P, the angle below m and to the right of t measures (x + 20)°. At R, the angle above n and to the right of t measures (2x + 10)°. Find x. What is the measure of the larger of the two given angles, in degrees?
hints: Between the lines, same side of t. What pair is that?
Same-side interior angles add to 180°: (x + 20) + (2x + 10) = 180.
Find x, then work out both angles and pick the bigger one.
quiz.solution:
Same-side interior → supplementary.
x + 20 + 2x + 10 = 180
3x + 30 = 180
x = 50
Angles: 50 + 20 = 70° and 2(50) + 10 = 110° → larger is 110°

figure.alt: Parallel lines m and n cut by transversal t at P and R. At P, the angle below the line, right of the transversal is labeled (x + 20) degrees. At R, the angle above the line, right of the transversal is labeled (2x + 10) degrees.
